title: The Knight Check on f6
subtitle: Opening the king with a sacrifice

source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter I, §4 Some Winning Positions in the Middle-game, Example 13

steps.title: Compensation, immediately
steps.source: Black has a R for a Kt and should therefore win, unless White is able to obtain some compensation immediately. White, in fact, mates in a few moves.

narration.say: Black is a rook for a knight ahead, and should win.
Unless White can do something right now. Look at the bishop on b2, aiming at the black king.
Your move. Give check with the knight.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Give a knight check.

feedback.*: The knight can give check from f6.

steps.title: Your turn: the open file
steps.source: Forced, otherwise Q x P mates.

narration.say: The capture was forced: otherwise queen takes h7 mates.
Now the g-file is open. Check the king.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Check along the g-file.

feedback.*: The queen can check on the g-file.

exercise.success: 2. Qg3, check. Black goes to h8.

exercise.prompt: White to move and give checkmate in one.

feedback.*: The bishop on the long diagonal can take with check.

exercise.success: Checkmate. Queen on the g-file, bishop on the long diagonal.

narration.say: A knight check on f6 can tear open the king's position.
Then queen and bishop combine along the open file and the long diagonal.
